solution: Core Reporting, Data Advisory, Value Creation

subsections.content: G3 is a specialist advisory firm operating in a high-trust, high-stakes environment, supporting clients through transactions, crises, disputes and complex geopolitical or reputational risks. Its model is built on selective, insight-driven judgement enabled by privileged human-source intelligence.

As the firm scales, it is increasingly constrained by fragmented data, inconsistent retention of critical human-source materials, and GDPR constraints that limit the use of unstructured inputs. The lack of linkage between project outputs and CRM information further reduces visibility over client dynamics and commercial performance. Collectively, these challenges create inefficiencies in reporting and limit ability to capitalise on AI.

G3 now needs a unified, compliant and robust data foundation that can streamline reporting today while enabling knowledge retrieval, workflow optimisation and other AI use cases tomorrow. The solution must be BAU-ready, scalable, and fully owned by G3. The immediate priorities are: Assessing where & how AI can be used to drive both top-line & bottom-line growth; and how this can be implemented with the relevant enablers (platform, governance, data). Implementing a data platform that acts as a single-source-of-truth, consolidating data from key systems across G3 and supporting automated reporting. JMAN’s two-phase approach responds directly to this need, enabling G3 to establish a robust foundation today while creating a clear pathway to expanded AI capability over time.

Option 1: Design & Discovery – Reporting Infrastructure & Point Solution AI Scoping (3 weeks)

Reporting Infrastructure

Commercial Deliverables

Business objectives & value levers: A document articulating G3’s strategic objectives and the key performance indicators required to measure them.

Metric & dimension dictionary: A clearly defined list of metrics across reporting use cases (e.g. client, project, etc.). The dictionary will also capture the dimensions important to drilling into G3’s performance (e.g. project type, project context). For the agreed priority reporting use case, detail will also be included on target calculation methodology and required data points.

Reporting design and dashboard mock-ups: Design of the insights and reports for the agreed priority reporting use case (e.g. client reporting, board pack). Visual mock-ups will capture layout, structure, and functionality requirements, serving as a blueprint for the implementation phase.

Delivery roadmap: A detailed plan outlining build-phase activities, milestones, and timelines for developing the foundational data platform and reporting outputs. The roadmap will be structured into prioritised, sprint-based phases to enable incremental delivery of use cases and value throughout the build.

Technical Deliverables

Data infrastructure and tooling recommendations: Recommendations for the foundational data platform and supporting tools required to deliver the initial reporting outputs. This will reflect JMAN’s assessment of G3’s current data environment, sources such as online systems (Sage, Salesforce), offline sources, and unstructured data (proposals, project materials, human-source interviews). Recommendations will also consider the platform’s scalability to support future growth and AI-enabled capabilities (e.g. AI-enabled automated redaction, expediting proposal/contract creation, etc.).

Conceptual data model: A high-level conceptual model outlining the structure & relationships of data to support the priority reporting use case.

Data assessment summary: A summary of initial observations on data availability, quality, and completeness to deliver the priority reporting use cases (e.g. Sage, Salesforce, etc.). The assessment will highlight key gaps, inform prioritisation of the build phase, and support future mitigation.

Point Solution AI Scoping

Commercial Deliverables

AI use case documentation: Identify, document & prioritise AI use cases across G3.

Process & workflow assessment: Targeted review of the workflow supporting the use case, highlighting manual steps, decision points and integration needs.

Value & feasibility snapshot: Full assessment of expected value (efficiency, cost, risk, accuracy) and high-level feasibility based on data readiness and system constraints.

POC concept: Defined POC scope, success criteria, required data, expected outputs and high-level solution approach for selected use case. We will also need to understand the GDPR compliance and how these considerations factor into the POC implementation.

Technical Deliverables

Data & system landscape assessment: A summary of the data, systems and architecture constraints relevant to delivering the selected AI use case, including Salesforce, Sage and unstructured sources such as proposals and project materials. This will highlight availability, quality, completeness and technical blockers.

Architectural alignment note: A short technical outline describing how the prioritised use case interacts with the proposed data and AI platform, ensuring that the POC concepts are deliverable within the future-state architecture.

Option 2 – Enterprise-wide AI Planning

Commercial Deliverables

Enterprise AI opportunity catalogue: A structured, business-wide register of all feasible and priority AI use cases across G3, including problem statements, underlying processes, data dependencies and expected business outcomes.

Cross-use-case process & workflow assessment: A consolidated view of workflows underpinning the identified opportunities, capturing decision points, manual touchpoints, bottlenecks and integration requirements that inform feasibility and design considerations.

Value & feasibility evaluation pack: A quantitative and qualitative assessment of all AI use cases’ potential commercial impact (efficiency gains, cost savings, risk reduction, revenue enablement) and a feasibility rating based on data availability, system readiness, and governance maturity.

Prioritisation & scoring framework: A transparent, reusable scoring model that evaluates each use case by impact, feasibility and strategic relevance. This becomes a repeatable asset for future AI prioritisation exercises.

Prioritised AI use case shortlist: A ranked set of AI opportunities derived from a structured prioritisation model, highlighting which use cases represent the highest near-term value and alignment to G3’s strategic objectives.

POC concepts for two priority use cases: A detailed concept design document describing the proposed POC scope, success criteria, required datasets, expected outputs, and high-level technical approach, forming the blueprint for Phase 2 delivery.

AI delivery roadmap: A phased delivery roadmap outlining milestones, dependencies, and timelines required to deliver the priority near-medium term POCs and foundational enablers. This will align with the broader platform development plan and position G3 for iterative AI delivery at scale.

Technical Deliverables

Data & system landscape assessment: A summary of the data, systems and architecture constraints relevant to delivering the identified AI use cases, including Salesforce, Sage and unstructured sources such as proposals and project materials. This will highlight availability, quality, completeness and technical blockers.

Architectural alignment note: A short technical outline describing how each prioritised use case interacts with the proposed data and AI platform, ensuring that the POC concepts are deliverable within the future-state architecture.

Phase 2 – Implementation

Key Deliverables

Foundational data platform: A robust, scalable data platform integrating structured data from Sage and Salesforce (and unstructured project content, to be determined by AI use case). The platform will include automated ingestion where possible and manual batch upload via templates for non-standard sources. It will be designed to support the metrics and KPIs defined for the agreed priority reporting use case and be expandable for future reporting and AI use cases.

Reporting outputs: Dashboards and visualisations to deliver the agreed metrics for the agreed priority reporting use case, providing visibility on growth, project performance, and client retention. These outputs will serve as the blueprint for ongoing operational reporting and AI-enabled insights.

Data quality & cleansing activities: Initial data cleansing of structured sources to ensure accuracy and usability of the priority reporting use case, including hierarchies and relationships across project, client, and contributor data. Further refinement will be implemented as the platform and reporting requirements evolve.

AI POC Implementation: Delivery of fully executed proof-of-concept for the pursued AI use cases, including development, testing, and validation of the model against agreed success criteria. The POC will demonstrate practical feasibility using real data, provide measurable performance results, and establish the technical foundations required to progress into MVP development and, ultimately, a production-ready solution.

Week 0

Pre-kick off workshop

JMAN recommends conducting 2 half-day workshops with key stakeholders within G3 and Oakley Capital (if relevant) to conduct a thorough deep dive on:

Business Model: Value proposition & customer segments, growth plans, risks & challenges, etc.

Reporting Infrastructure: Tools in use, structured and unstructured data sources (e.g. Sage, Salesforce, proposals, project material, human-source interviews), existing reporting (e.g. board pack, operational reporting, etc.).

Ahead of the workshops, it would be helpful for G3 to provide any existing example reporting.

Pre-kick off requirements

The below details access and materials that should be shared with JMAN ahead of project kick-off to ensure the JMAN team have access to all necessary materials during the project.

Data access: Work with G3 to arrange access to Salesforce and Sage (& other agreed systems), plus any existing reports being generated on this data.

Data extracts: Sample data extracts from the existing source systems.

Data architecture / infrastructure documentation: Liaise with internal technical stakeholders to receive all the existing documentation for reporting, infrastructure & systems landscape, and tech stack configurations, where these exist.

Existing reporting and requirements: Understand existing reports shared, including meetings with report owners to understand existing process.

Weeks 1-3 – Define reporting metrics & architecture

Objective: Define target metrics, design the foundational data platform and architecture, identify list of AI use cases; gain a clear understanding of Salesforce and Sage against the target data model considering data availability & quality.

Metric dictionary & reporting use cases: Document detailed definitions for target metrics, including calculation logic and data points required to support the agreed priority reporting use case. Align on broader metrics and future reporting opportunities.

Confirm dimensions: Identify how G3 wants to segment the business for reporting narratives and create a list of required dimensions (e.g., service type, geography).

Reporting design: Produce dashboard summaries and visual mock-ups for the first reporting outputs, serving as the blueprint for implementation and highlighting potential additional reports for future phases.

Data & AI platform selection and architecture design: Recommend the foundational platform and supporting tools to integrate structured and unstructured data and provide scalable architecture to support AI capabilities.

Design target data model: Highlight the required relationships between data points in the platform to be able to execute and create the calculation logic for the agreed priority reporting use case.

Data gap assessment: Provide a feasibility check of Sage & Salesforce’s available data to ensure deliverability on requirements from metric dictionary. Identify any data gaps for existing & historical data – share recommendations for how these gaps can be filled both historically and going forwards.

Week 3 – Develop phased delivery plan

Objective: Develop a prioritised roadmap for delivering the priority reporting outputs and AI POC agreed during Phase 1 that will be delivered during the implementation phase of the project (Phase 2)

Platform & Reporting Implementation plan: Outline phased delivery for reporting outputs and infrastructure build, including timelines, milestones, and resource requirements.

Acceleration opportunities & tooling: Identify ways to expedite delivery and advise on tools and services to support platform setup and smooth transition into implementation.

Weeks 1-3 – Targeted AI Use Case Prioritisation

Objective: Identify potential AI use cases, prioritise a single near-term opportunity, and define the scope and requirements for a proof-of-concept (POC).

AI use case identification: Identify and document the full list of potential AI use cases across the business.

Prioritise AI use cases: Prioritise the first target use case for POC implementation from the documented long list.

Subsequent design phase scoping activities will then vary according to the use case – e.g. chatbot vs agentic AI. It will likely consist of the below:

Process and workflow review: Map the end-to-end workflow for the prioritised use case, capturing decision points, data inputs, handoffs, and the underlying pain points or constraints that limit performance today.

Value and feasibility assessment: Assess efficiency gains, cost reduction and quality improvements, and evaluate feasibility based on data availability, system readiness and governance considerations.

POC design: Define the scope, success criteria, required data, and technical approach for delivering a POC for the prioritised use case.

Week 3 – Develop phased delivery plan

Objective: Develop a prioritised roadmap for delivering the AI POC agreed during Phase 1 that will be delivered during the implementation phase of the project (Phase 2)

AI Use Case POC Implementation plan: Define the phased delivery of the prioritised AI use case POC, including key milestones, dependencies, and validation checkpoints to guide the subsequent build and rollout.

Week 0

Pre-kick off workshop

JMAN recommends conducting 2 half-day workshops with key stakeholders within G3 and Oakley Capital (if relevant) to conduct a thorough deep dive on:

Business and Operating Model Overview: Review G3’s service lines, core workflows, client engagement model, growth priorities, and known operational or information bottlenecks.

AI readiness context: Align on where AI could support core activities, the nature of unstructured materials, and any constraints related to privacy, governance or ways of working.

Ahead of these workshops, it would be helpful for G3 to provide any documentation that outlines existing data flows or processes.

Pre-kick off requirements

The below details access and materials that should be shared with JMAN ahead of project kick-off to ensure the JMAN team have access to all necessary materials during the project.

Data access: Work with G3 to arrange access to Salesforce and Sage (& other agreed systems), plus any existing reports being generated on this data.

Data extracts: Sample data extracts from the existing source systems.

Data architecture / infrastructure documentation: Liaise with internal technical stakeholders to receive all the existing documentation for reporting, infrastructure & systems landscape, and tech stack configurations, where these exist.

Existing process documentation: Understand existing operational processes, including meetings with ops leads.

Weeks 1-6 – Enterprise-Wide AI Use Case Assessment

Objective: Identify and document all potential AI use cases across G3, assess each for business value and feasibility, and complete conceptual design for two priority POCs.

Enterprise use case catalogue: Develop a structured register of AI opportunities across all functions, capturing core activities, problem statements, and relevant data inputs.

Process and workflow assessment: Review the underlying workflows for each opportunity to identify decision points, manual effort, bottlenecks and data dependencies that influence suitability for AI.

GDPR evaluation: Assess GDPR and broader data privacy requirements relevant to each use case, including how regulations impact data access, preprocessing, retention, and workflows. Identify compliance constraints, required safeguards, and any implications for model development, deployment, and future scalability.

Value and feasibility evaluation: Quantify potential efficiency gains, commercial impact and risk reduction per use case, and assess delivery feasibility based on data, systems and governance maturity.

Use case prioritisation: Apply a structured prioritisation model to rank opportunities by impact, feasibility and alignment with G3’s strategic objectives, resulting in a shortlist for near-term delivery.

POC concept development (two use cases): For the two highest-priority opportunities, define the proposed POC approach, including scope, required datasets, success criteria, high-level technical architecture and any dependencies on platform components.

Alignment with platform design: Confirm how each prioritised use case will link into the proposed data and AI platform architecture, ensuring the conceptual POC designs are technically deliverable within the roadmap.

Week 6 – Develop phased delivery plan

Objective: Develop a prioritised roadmap for delivering the AI capabilities agreed during Phase 1 that will be delivered during the implementation phase of the project (Phase 2)

AI Use Case POC Implementation plan: Translate both POC concepts into a structured delivery plan, including phased milestones, data and engineering dependencies, validation and acceptance checkpoints, and integration considerations with the developing data platform.

Acceleration opportunities & tooling: Identify ways to expedite delivery and advise on tools and services to support platform setup and smooth transition into implementation.

The following outlines the key outcomes expected in Phase 2; these will be further detailed by JMAN prior to starting development in collaboration with G3.

Foundational data platform: A robust, scalable data platform integrating structured data from Sage and Salesforce (and unstructured project content, to be determined by AI use case). The platform will include automated ingestion where possible and manual batch upload via templates for non-standard sources. It will be designed to support the metrics and KPIs defined for the agreed priority reporting use case and be expandable for future reporting and AI use cases.

Reporting outputs: Dashboards and visualisations to deliver the agreed metrics for the agreed priority reporting use case, providing visibility on growth, project performance, and client retention. These outputs will serve as the blueprint for ongoing operational reporting and AI-enabled insights.

Data quality & cleansing activities: Initial data cleansing of structured sources to ensure accuracy and usability of the priority reporting use case, including hierarchies and relationships across project, client, and contributor data. Further refinement will be implemented as the platform and reporting requirements evolve.

AI POC Implementation: Delivery of fully executed proof-of-concept for the pursued AI use cases, including development, testing, and validation of the model against agreed success criteria. The POC will demonstrate practical feasibility using real data, provide measurable performance results, and establish the technical foundations required to progress into MVP development and, ultimately, a production-ready solution.

Phased approach – ensures the highest priority items are delivered first, focusing on the board pack first-use case and foundational metrics, while capturing requirements for broader reporting and AI capabilities.

Expertise in diverse data maturity landscape – JMAN has extensive experience working with extremely acquisitive businesses, with a broad range of data maturities (e.g. Excel-based to system-based reporting).

Single-Source-of-Truth data and reporting – across the complex data landscape and multiple brands, this approach leaves G3 with a granular, consolidated, single-source-of-truth data asset that is the foundation for data-led decision-making.

Future-proofed platform – a data platform and reporting suite are designed to scale with G3’s growth, support AI-enabled workflows (e.g., proposal enrichment, contributor matching, business development insights), and adapt as operational requirements evolve.

Specialist PE-backed experience – JMAN’s track record with private equity portfolio companies ensures G3’s data environment will be built to scale, evolve, and withstand scrutiny in future growth or exit events, including being the only provider to be named explicitly in the data category of an exit (Dains exit from Horizon in 2024).
